help.title: About Leads
help.overview: A Lead is a person in the commercial pipeline before a reservation or sale exists. It is CRM, not a lock on a unit. Status is a sales-stage label you update as you work the person; it does not change unit availability. Winning a lead does not create a reservation — you create that on Reservations from an available unit.

sections.title: What a lead holds
items: First name (required), optional last name, email, phone.
Status: new → contacted → qualified → proposal → negotiation → won or lost.
Source: website, referral, social, event, cold call, walk-in, chat, or other.
Interest: partnerships, investments, platform support, reservation, or other.
Optional project interest and unit interest — what they asked about, not a hold.
Optional budget and budget currency, free-text notes, assigned agent, follow-up date.
Activity log — timestamped notes from the “add activity” action (who did what).

sections.title: On this page
items: Create a lead as soon as someone enquires. Assign an agent and set a follow-up date if you work a queue.
Open the card to move status, add notes, and log activity.
Filter by status, source, project, assignee.
Soft delete can be restored. It does not cancel reservations that were created later for the same person.

sections.title: How it behaves
items: A lead can point at a unit that is already reserved or sold — that is only “interest”, not a conflict check.
There is no automatic conversion from lead to reservation. When they are ready, create a Reservation with a client user on an available unit.
Won / lost are pipeline outcomes. They do not write Unit status.
Public website or chat can create leads (source website / chat) depending on how the company is configured.

sections.title: Related records
items: Next commercial documents: Reservation, then Sale; or a Lease if they rent instead.
Agent report later counts reservations and sales, not lead stages.
